data.why: The repo ships bundled count/metadata CSVs for QC and profiling, but no sample DESeq2/edgeR/limma result files, so synthetic DE result tables (60 genes, matching the gene IDs in test_data/counts.csv) were written to exercise Import DE, Ensemble, and Threshold Optimization: 10 strongly concordant DE genes, 10 genes significant in DESeq2/edgeR but not limma (tests ensemble disagreement), 38 null genes, one extreme-logFC/high-SE outlier, and one gene with all-NaN stats (failed test).

goals: Upload a raw count matrix and sample metadata, run quality assessment, and identify outlier samples and batch effects before proceeding to differential expression
Profile the dataset's 32 statistical features (BCV, dispersion, sparsity) and get a pipeline recommendation
Import DE results from DESeq2, edgeR, and limma, letting RAPTOR auto-detect the tool and standardize columns
Combine the three DE result sets into a consensus call using Fisher's, Brown's, RRA, Voting, or Weighted ensemble methods and compare which genes replicate across methods
Tune significance thresholds (FDR, logFC) interactively using data-driven methods (FDR control, stability, reproducibility) instead of arbitrary cutoffs
Export a consensus gene list and publication-ready report

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately, its labels are clean, and every one of the 11 cited screens I opened shows what its node claims. But its central result, a consensus gene list, was never produced, almost certainly because the run's own synthetic data included an all-NaN gene, and the optimization and ensemble phases are in the wrong order. Re-run the ensemble step without that gene, reorder the phases, add export/report and threshold-method coverage, and finish the replay check before filing.
